journal.action: The current-Mathlib PlaneMap stack now proves closed-walk face-sum parity, alternating-walk Heawood separation, degree-five neighbour rotation, and five_color_extension across any deleted vertex of degree at most five. DeleteVertex proves strict component-size decrease and colouring assembly; FiveColorExamples proves every PlaneMap 6 is five-colourable. The global five_color_theorem remains open on generated PlaneMap reconstruction for deleted components and a recursive low-degree premise that does not assume face-length preservation. This is not the Four Colour Theorem.

patches.approach: The local topological and Kempe extension stack is complete on current Mathlib. Finish the global theorem by reconstructing generated PlaneMaps for deleted components, transporting colourability across finite relabelings, and proving a hereditary recursive degree-at-most-five interface. Keep the five-to-four problem separate.

notes.text: The Five Colour route uses a closed walk directly. No ConnectedCycleCut constructor or global cycle_two_sides theorem is required.

patches.title: Closed-walk Heawood separation bridge
patches.statement: For cyclically ordered, distinctly coloured neighbours of a degree-five vertex, bichromatic reachability for the first alternating pair excludes reachability for the second pair after deleting the centre.
patches.approach: Close the first bichromatic walk through the centre, express its mod-two edge multiplicity as a face sum, and propagate face coefficients along any disjoint second walk. The odd middle boundary edge gives a contradiction.

notes.text: The connected-cycle proposal is superseded for this application by the more direct closed-walk parity argument.

patches.evidence: heawood_hopposite and degree_five_neighbour_rotation compile. PlaneMap/FiveColor.lean bridges actual Kempe bichromatic reachability to the induced-graph statement and proves five_color_extension.

patches.title: Generated component reconstruction after deletion
patches.statement: After deleting a vertex, every connected component is strictly smaller and colourings assemble; the remaining task is to represent each component, up to finite relabeling, by a generated PlaneMap suitable for strong induction.
patches.approach: Reuse the proved graph-level deletion API. Construct rotation restrictions and Fin m relabelings componentwise, then prove Generated from construction history or adopt a carrier redesign with a proved equivalence.

notes.text: Deletion may disconnect. Strict size decrease and colouring assembly are proved; Generated component closure and colourability transport across relabeling are not.

patches.title: Five Colour Theorem in Lean
patches.statement: Every generated PlaneMap has a proper Fin 5 vertex colouring.
patches.approach: Use strong induction with five_color_extension and the proved component assembly. Supply generated component PlaneMaps and a recursive degree-at-most-five interface without assuming face-length preservation under deletion.
